newsitem.title: CANADA: UGG sees W.Canada grains losing ground to oilseeds.
newsitem.headline: UGG sees W.Canada grains losing ground to oilseeds.

text.p: United Grain Growers said it expects less area to be seeded to cereals this spring than last, but oilseeds and special crops should gain land in 1997/98 (Aug/July).
UGG forecast wheat acreage would total 27.393 million acres, down 11 percent from Statistics Canada's 1996/97 estimate of 30.725 million acres.

"Wheat will be a matter of international values. Wheat's slid quite dramatically from where it was last year. We're going with the Wheat Board being so far behind in its exports this year, said UGG analyst, Mike Jubinville.
"Farmers will be carrying a lot of inventory," Jubinville added.
The Canadian Wheat Board last month said it was 1.5 million tonnes behind in its export program due to ship backlogs on the Pacific Coast.
The UGG estimates were based on a survey of elevator managers conducted March 17-19.
Canola acreage in western Canada this year was projected at 12.166 million acres, up 38 percent from the prior year which StatsCan's 1996/97 estimate set at 8.802 million.
Trade expectations had set canola area around 13 million.
"Canola doesn't look all that attractive when you look at new crop values. Alternatives like barley, oats and flax are giving canola the run for its money," Jubinville said.

"Canola seed sales have been slower than expected but I suspect there'll be a rush ahead of seeding and that'll probably bring the number up on canola and it'll steal away from the barley and oat areas," Jubinville added.
Barley area in western Canada was forecast at 11.83 million acres, down five percent from StatsCan's 1996/97 estimate of 12.40 million acres.

Oat area in western Canada this year was projected at 4.529 million acres, down five percent from StatsCan's 1996/97 estimate of 4.785 million acres. Flax area on the Prairies was forecast at 2.098 million acres, up 41 percent from 1.490.
Special crop area was forecast to rise in western Canada to 3.987 million acres, up 18 percent from StatsCan's 1996/97 estimate of 3.391 million acres.
